messages:
Maria (PM): Quick design-review: API keys list — I think the proximity of Revoke to Copy is causing accidental revokes in our usability tests. Can we rework affordances? :thinking:
Alex (Design): Agreed. Two quick ideas: 1) move Revoke into an overflow menu, 2) make Revoke a red secondary button with confirmation toast + undo. Prefer overflow for safety.
Samir (Frontend): Overflow is easy, but we lose discoverability for power users. Maybe put Revoke behind an icon with a hover label and require a confirm modal.
Priya (Accessibility): If we hide it in overflow, ensure the menu is keyboard reachable and has clear aria-labels. Also keyboard undo should be announced by screen readers.
Maria (PM): Good call. We should balance discoverability vs safety. What about a prominent Revoke for admin roles and overflow for others? Role-based affordances.
Jules (Eng): Role-based is doable but increases complexity in the client. Alternative: keep a visible '...' menu with top-level Revoke for admins, and a muted inline link for everyone else.
Alex (Design): Mocked a couple options, attaching text (will post screenshots in a follow-up thread). For copy: instead of "Revoke", try "Revoke key" or "Disable key" — which communicates intent better?
Samir (Frontend): "Disable key" implies reversible, "Revoke" feels permanent. We have undo for a short window, so maybe "Disable" is more accurate.
Priya (Accessibility): Language parity matters for screen readers. Use consistent verbs across flows: Create / Disable / Rotate. Also ensure confirmation modal has role="alertdialog" and focus trap.
Maria (PM): Rotation flow: current microcopy says "Overwrite existing key" — that's confusing. Proposed: "Rotate key: creates a new secret and invalidates the old one after confirmation." Shorten text on the row to "Rotates secret; old key invalidated."
Alex (Design): Also we flagged the empty state: when a user has no keys and limited permissions, we should explain why the CTA is disabled. e.g., "Create key (requires admin role)" with a tooltip linking to permissions docs.
Priya (Accessibility): Tooltip must be keyboard-triggerable and accessible. For disabled CTA, include an inline explanation in the DOM, not only a tooltip.
Jules (Eng): Quick note on undo: we currently soft-delete on server for 10 minutes. If UX wants an undo toast with an action, we can do that, but the toast must persist long enough (10s?) and be focusable for screen readers.
Maria (PM): UX asks for an explicit 30s undo window visual on the toast. Is that acceptable backend-wise?
Jules (Eng): 30s persisted soft-delete okay. We throttle mass-revokes though. Bulk revoke still needs a confirmation step listing N keys.
Alex (Design): Bulk flow: make the confirmation step emphasize the number of services/tokens that may fail. Show a checklist: backup configs, rotate dependent tokens.
Priya (Accessibility): For the bulk modal, include a summary at top and a clear primary CTA with aria-describedby linking to the summary. Also keyboard first focus should be on the primary button only after user reads summary.
Samir (Frontend): CSS nit: row density is tight. If we add overflow menu and badges (role, last used), rows should get slightly taller. We'll need to adjust responsive layout for mobile.
Maria (PM): Good. Action items: Alex to post mocks; Priya to produce aria checklist; Samir/Jules to estimate frontend + backend changes; I'll draft copy alternatives. Can we also add a small inline microcopy below the table for "last used" meaning? People keep misreading it.
Alex (Design): noted — will include tooltip and short line: "Last used: time when key was last used for inference or management API."
ConsentBot: Reminder: please add any UX changes affecting data retention or audit logs to the compliance ticket #C-412.
Maria (PM): Thanks — I'll link the ticket in the follow-up. :thumbsup:
